title: Build your first CTRLbot system
subtitle: From a device driver to a client-ready control interface
learningObjectives: Choose a driver from the catalog
Create and test a secure connection
Hand off a simplified End User Interface

chapters.title: 1. Choose a device driver
chapters.narration: Start in Device Drivers. Search by manufacturer, choose the matching control profile, and confirm the supported model and command set.
bullets: Verify IP, serial, or IR control
chapters.callout: Start with the exact model whenever possible

chapters.title: 2. Configure the connection
chapters.narration: Give the device a room-friendly label, enter its address and port, then test the connection before saving it.
bullets: Select TCP, Telnet, SSH, RS-232, or IR
chapters.callout: Credentials are referenced securely—not stored in plaintext

chapters.title: 3. Build a preset
chapters.narration: Combine commands and delays into an ordered workflow. Test the sequence, then make it available to the operator.
chapters.callout: A preset should always end in a known state

chapters.title: 4. Switch to the End User Interface
chapters.narration: The End User Interface turns installer configuration into a simplified, kiosk-style control surface for the client.
chapters.callout: Press and hold the top-left control for two seconds to return to Setup

closing: Your first system is ready to control
